label: Per se necessary esse, modal proxy (PER_SE_NECESSARY_1)
term: per se necessary esse, modal proxy
definition: An esse principle e is necessary at world w in the modal proxy sense when the same e satisfies the esse-existence predicate at w and at every world accessible from w. Its negation for a conjunction is ContingentConjunctionAt: the joining holds at w but fails at some accessible world. No cause, dependence or grounding relation occurs in this sense.
note: The rendering of n.3's 'per se necesse' used by the first-case formalization of PR #1602 (definition b18c2550-e953-42d4-817c-cc6805cf5004). It is an analyst proxy: SCG I's per se/per aliud distinction concerns whether something has a cause of its necessity, which this sense omits; see the sibling dependence sense d9716c00-9d36-4814-9ee5-456eb0bf7dce. The modal and dependence senses are not related in either direction in the corpus: a permanent but dependent union is not modally contingent (finite control in Chapter22SecondCase), and nothing is asserted about whether an esse without a cause of its necessity is present at every world.
